stages.name: Cost of regional trade agreements
stages.title: Cost of regional trade agreements
stages.sub: Understand why joining a regional trade agreement can mean giving up national control over policy.

steps.q: Before joining a currency union, a country sets its own interest rates and its own trade rules to suit its own economy. Once it joins a deep trade agreement, can it still set all of these entirely alone?
steps.right: No, some choices are now made together
steps.wrong: Yes, every choice is still its own
steps.hint: Think about what a currency union like the Eurozone actually requires members to agree on.
steps.pre: So before joining, a country is used to

steps.q: Members of a trade bloc agree common tariffs, standards and sometimes a common currency. If one member wants a different tariff to protect its own farmers, can it just set one?
steps.right: No, it must follow the agreed common rules
steps.wrong: Yes, each member sets its own tariffs freely
steps.hint: The whole point of the bloc is that members agree the same rules together.

steps.q: A recession hits one member country hard, but the bloc's shared interest rate and trade rules were set to suit the average of all members. Can that country change the shared rules just for itself?
steps.right: No, its own needs can be overruled by the group
steps.wrong: Yes, it can override the rules for its own case
steps.hint: The rules were agreed by all members together, not by one country alone.

steps.q: So when a country joins a deep trade agreement and hands control of tariffs, standards or its currency to a shared body, what has it given up?
steps.right: Some control over its own economic decisions
steps.wrong: Only a small amount of trade with outsiders
steps.hint: Think about who now decides the rules the country once decided for itself.
